title: Rural life advantages; commuting to Moscow; rural vs urban women
description: Rebecca Kellom describes the advantages of living in rural Bovill, Idaho, including the safety of children roaming freely and the isolation from city life. She discusses the challenges of commuting to Moscow for work and compares the self-reliance required of rural women versus urban women.

title: Childhood during the Depression; family life; education
description: Kellom recounts her childhood during the Depression, moving frequently as her father searched for work. She describes playing baseball, climbing trees, and other childhood activities, as well as her mother's emphasis on education despite having only an eighth-grade education herself.

title: Courtship and marriage; logging camp life
description: Kellom describes meeting her husband Dallas in Bovill, their courtship, and their early married life. She explains the challenges of logging camp life, where Dallas worked for months at a time, and the hardships of managing finances during layoffs.

title: Childbirth accident; medical emergencies
description: Kellom recounts the traumatic birth of her daughter Denise, which occurred during a car accident en route to the hospital. She also describes handling medical crises alone while her husband was at camp, including a hepatitis outbreak and a medication error that nearly killed her daughter.

title: Children's futures; wartime travel
description: Kellom shares her hopes for her daughters' futures, including marriages and careers. She concludes by describing her family's journey from Arkansas to Washington by train during World War II, including a memorable experience riding on a troop train.
